name: OMA
author: Stephan Kaufmann
description: Local knowledge. Ask your own documents and see where every answer comes from.

schema.label: Backend when OMA is closed
schema.description: Closing the window releases the loaded models — but only once a question that is still running has finished, so an answer started before closing is never cut short. Stop with OMA also takes the server down when the shell exits; the next question waits for it to come back. Keep running holds the server, roughly 430 MB, past that and leaves loaded models in place until they time out, so the next question starts straight away.

schema.label: Answering model
schema.description: Passed to `lilbee ask --model`. Leave empty to use whatever lilbee is configured with. Useful when the configured model is too large to load next to the retrieval models.

schema.label: Text size
schema.description: A factor on the shell's text sizes, applied inside OMA only. 1.0 is exactly what the rest of Omarchy uses. The shell's own font is never changed.

schema.label: Font
schema.description: Font family for OMA alone. Leave empty to follow the shell's font, which is what `omarchy font set` configures.

schema.label: Sound when an answer arrives
schema.description: Played only when the answer finishes while OMA is closed. Any file the desktop can play; leave empty for silence. Setup offers herdr's own notification sound, which OMA lifts out of the installed herdr binary because herdr ships it compiled in.

schema.label: Compact window
schema.description: Opens a small window under the bar icon showing the chat alone, instead of the large one in the middle of the screen. The icon in the header switches between them.

schema.label: Window opacity
schema.description: How solid the window's background is, from 1.0 for opaque down to 0.45. Only the background fades — the text stays fully legible, because this is a window for reading numbers out of a textbook.

schema.label: Keep free (GiB)
schema.description: How much memory OMA leaves for everything else. Empty means six percent of this machine's RAM, never under 2 GiB. OMA will not start a load that would eat into it, and gives its models back when the kernel reports that something else is stalling on memory. Where llama-manager is installed, its own reserve is used instead and this is ignored.
